---
title: "Plausibility checks"
description: "How OPDI leaves out events that the aircraft's own track clearly contradicts, before anything is published."
---

## In one sentence

The plausibility checks remove, before publication, the events that the
aircraft's own position reports clearly contradict, such as an in-block time
while the aircraft is still flying.

## What it needs

- All events of the track, once every detector has run.
- The reports of the same track within 60 s before and after each event: the
  height above the airport, the ground speed and the ground flag.

## How it is computed

1. **What the aircraft was doing.** For each event read by a check, take the
   height above the airport of the nearest report with an altitude, the
   ground speed of the nearest report with a speed, and whether any report
   within 60 s is flagged on the ground. The airport is the one the event
   names; otherwise the departure airport for `AOBT` and `ATOT`, the
   destination airport for `AIBT` and `ALDT`, and the nearer of the two for
   the others.
2. **The checks**, in this order; the first that fires removes the event:

   | Check | Events read | Removed when |
   |---|---|---|
   | No time | every event type | the event has no time |
   | Ground event while flying | `AOBT`, `AIBT`, `entry-{element}`, `exit-{element}` | more than 1,500 ft above the airport (15,000 ft altitude when the airport is unknown), faster than 80 kt, and no report on the ground within 60 s |
   | Runway time too high | `ATOT`, `ALDT` | more than 1,500 ft above the ground at the airport |
   | Off-block after take-off | `AOBT` | at or after the take-off of its own part of the track |
   | In-block before landing | `AIBT` | at or before the landing of its own part of the track |

3. **Height of a take-off or landing time.** The event's altitude, or the
   altitude interpolated between the nearest reports either side within 10 s,
   minus the track's own altitude on the ground at that airport (the median of
   its reports flagged on the ground with an altitude, within 30 minutes and
   5 NM). Without such reports the airport's elevation is used and 1,000 ft is
   added to the limit, for the error of barometric altitude on a day of low
   pressure (about 27 ft per hPa).
4. **Only clear evidence removes an event.** A check fires only when every
   fact it needs is known; when one is unknown, the event is kept.

A removed event is not published, its measurements go with it, and it is not
used for the milestone columns of the flight list.

## Based on

Developed for OPDI and measured in
[Plausibility checks for flight milestones](../../papers/milestone-plausibility-v1/index.html).

## What is published

Nothing of its own: the checks decide which events are published.

## Use cases

- **Trust the order of milestones**: in the published data an off-block time
  never follows the take-off of its own leg, nor an in-block time precede its
  landing.

## Limitations

The checks cannot see an event that is wrong but plausible, such as a block
time a few minutes off. See
[Limitations: general](../limitations.qmd#general-limits).

## Availability and accuracy

Not an item of its own; the study below measures how many events the checks
remove and how many of them the airport records confirm.
